payload.purpose_context: spec-kitty's merge and abort lifecycle fires destructive git commands (reset --hard, worktree remove --force, merge --abort) against the operator's primary checkout and lane worktrees with no dirty/branch/state guard, silently deleting uncommitted work with a success exit (issues #4752, #4753, #4754). This mission closes that data-loss class by unifying a refuse-before-destroy guard.
payload.purpose_tldr: Stop spec-kitty merge and merge --abort from silently destroying uncommitted user work

options: Patch each of the three sites independently
payload.question: Should the three destructive-op bugs be fixed by unifying one refuse-before-destroy guard primitive, or by patching each site independently?

payload.final_answer: Unify a shared refuse-before-destroy guard primitive (modeled on git/ref_advance._dirty_entries + a typed RefAdvance-style refusal), routed through the destructive sites. Grounding squad found ~9 forked dirty-check predicates with no canonical owner (file-lock-authority-gap-shaped); patch-3 would mint a 10th and guarantee the next whack-a-field. Operator-delegated answer from grounding findings.

options: Fold coupled coord-teardown + orchestrator-api worktree-remove mirror through the guarded seam; defer branch -D
